$comment: ADOPTION MANIFEST (arch step 2, S0) — CONTRACT-INTENT-FACTS-DESIGN-2026-07-26 §'The adoption rule'.
THE RULE: no field ships without, in the same change train, a named producer with a
producer-verified test, a named consumer with a consumer-verified test, or an explicit
dark-state entry carrying a removal date.
WHY: this estate already shipped three meaning fields with no producer at all. Nothing
failed, so nobody noticed across two minor versions. The rows below record that failure
as measured fact, not as a plan. Enforced by scripts/check-adoption-manifest.mjs.
WHAT COUNTS AS A PRODUCER TEST: a test that FAILS if the producer stops emitting the
field. A test asserting the field is OPTIONAL on the wire is not a producer test.
WHAT COUNTS AS A CONSUMER TEST: a test that FAILS if the consumer stops USING the value.
A test asserting the field survives parsing is a transport test, not a consumer test —
it passes just as happily when the value is parsed and then thrown away. Transport-only
evidence goes in `notes`, never in `producer_test`/`consumer_test`. Conflating the two
is how a field reaches `enforced` while still being decorative.
EVIDENCE BASIS: counted 2026-07-26 against each repo's authoritative_ref in repo-map.json
(staging for the four services, main for schemas), NOT against main. Positive control:
`assistant_text` = 543 files / 3815 lines in CEE staging, 117 files / 533 lines in UI
staging, so the counting method demonstrably finds producers when they exist.

states.declared: the field exists in the contract; no verified producer and no verified consumer
states.produced_dark: a producer emits it behind a flag/dark, with a producer test; no verified consumer
states.consumed_dark: a consumer reads it behind a flag/dark, with a consumer test; no verified producer
states.enforced: both sides verified by named tests; the field may be made required

notes: ADOPTED 2026-07-26 — this row moved `declared` → `enforced` when CEE PR #712 merged
(cee@staging 820f3e83b, deployed). It is the first row in this manifest to reach
`enforced`, and the evidence was held to the same bar that keeps `assistant_text`
at `produced_dark`: both references below are the right KIND of test, not transport pins.
PRODUCER TEST — drives the REAL run_analysis handler and asserts the VALUE of
`fact.result.constraint_verdict` on BOTH verdict answers. The cited `it` is the
discriminating control: without it a producer hard-coding
`{ may_name_leading_option: false }` would pass. Its siblings in the same describe
add the drift bolt (the field is never absent, on either verdict) and assert the
interim key is GONE, so the interim cannot become permanent by neglect.
CONSUMER TEST — drives the REAL Fastify route through the REAL compose/finalise path
and asserts on the SERIALISED HTTP BYTES. The cited `it` is a POSITIVE CONTROL: on a
permitted run the leader id, the enrichment blobs and the decision brief must all
ride the wire. Note the DIRECTION — if the reader stopped consulting
`result.constraint_verdict` it would fall through to the (now never-written) interim
key and fail CLOSED, so the withhold assertions in that suite would still pass and
only this positive control would go red. A consumer test for a fail-closed reader
MUST be the permitting case; the withholding case cannot discriminate.
SECOND, INDEPENDENT CONSUMER PROOF (not cited above, one ref per column): §2 of the
producer file pins the reader's precedence ladder directly — typed field first,
interim second, closed third, with the typed field winning over a disagreeing interim
in BOTH directions and a malformed typed field refusing to fall through.

DECLARED, and `declared` is the whole truth about it: as of this release NOTHING emits
an analysis fact and NOTHING reads one. The field exists in the contract, optional,
with no producer and no consumer — which is exactly this manifest's definition of

SCOPE MEASURED, not assumed, at schemas main tip e048e353 (0.26.0, the parent of this
change): `git grep -nE 'AnalysisFact|analysis_facts|SuppressedFact|UnavailableFact|
ComputedFact'` over the tip AND all 23 remote branch tips returns exactly ONE hit,
and it is PROSE, not code — CHANGELOG.md:64, 0.26.0's own 'the row belongs to the
`population` field itself, which lands with S1's ComputedFact'. So: zero declarations,
zero producers, zero consumers, one recorded expectation (honoured by this release and
by the sibling row below). There is no prior shape to migrate and no consumer to break.
WHY IT IS A UNION AND NOT A `status` FIELD (Codex contract step-2 finding F3, P1): a
flat status beside a separate value map lets `status:'suppressed'` and a still-present
plausible number BOTH parse. `ComputedFact` REQUIRES `value`; `UnavailableFact` and
`SuppressedFact` do not declare it and are `.strict()`, so a withheld metric carrying
a number FAILS TO PARSE. tests/contracts/analysis-fact.test.ts keeps the flat shape
checked in as a BLIND CONTROL and asserts, case by case, that it accepts what the
union rejects.
NOT A PRODUCER TEST, and deliberately not cited as one: the tests in this repo are
SCHEMA tests — they prove the shape rejects a dishonest fact. They would pass
unchanged if no service ever emitted one, which is the state today. Per this
manifest's own test-KIND rule that evidence belongs here, in `notes`, and never in
`producer_test`/`consumer_test`.
DISCLOSED LIMIT, asserted rather than left to be discovered: `win_probabilities` and
the other legacy maps are RETAINED for the compatibility window, so a producer
emitting BOTH can still contradict a suppressed fact via the legacy map. The union
makes the dishonest state unrepresentable WITHIN A FACT; it does not delete the map.
Removing the maps is a later change train, gated on a verified consumer of the facts.
Pinned by 'DISCLOSED LIMIT — the legacy map can still contradict a suppressed fact'.
ADOPTION PATH: readers first (design of record §'Adoption order'). CEE is the only
service that can produce these — it owns the compute-orchestration seam and the
persisted run_analysis fact this field hangs on. When a producer lands, this row
moves to `produced_dark` with a test that FAILS if the producer stops emitting; a UI
consumer moves it to `enforced` only with a test that FAILS if the value stops being
USED. Neither exists yet, and the date above is the dead-man's switch on that.

SEQUENCING (ROADMAP 2.258, and the ORDER is the safety property, not a preference):

Re-landing the plumbing before the converter would resurrect the structural-zero '< 1%'

PRODUCER WHEN IT LANDS: cee — goal-threshold-cap.ts single mint site, stamped as a CODE
CONSTANT. It must NEVER be added to a drafting prompt's output surface: the frame is a
property of the minting arithmetic, not of the user's phrasing.
CONSUMER WHEN IT LANDS: isl — the single goal-comparison site (it alone knows its sample
frame and holds the observed_state baselines). Forwarding is TRANSPORT and would not
qualify PLoT as the consumer for this row in any case.
⚠ CORRECTED AFTER ADVERSARIAL REVIEW — THIS ROW PREVIOUSLY CLAIMED 'plot forwards verbatim'
AND THAT IS FALSE. Verified at PLoT tip 9beb4229: toISLNode (translator-v3.ts:233-242) is a
SIX-FIELD CONSTRUCTOR and ISL_DECLARED_OBSERVED_STATE_FIELDS is a TEN-MEMBER ALLOW-LIST;
neither carries goal_threshold_frame. The :534 cite that travelled with the claim is the
goal_threshold SCALAR line, not a node-level passthrough.
PLoT MUST ADD FORWARDING — either extend toISLNode or carry a request-level scalar beside
goal_threshold. It rides the 2.258 PLoT stint and is a PRECONDITION for the ISL converter
being reachable at all. BOTH PLoT-side lists are HAND-MAINTAINED ALLOW-LISTS with NO
FAIL-LOUD on a new contract field, so a field added here is silently dropped there and the
drift reads as green — the estate's dominant defect class, sitting directly on this train.
Until forwarding lands, a stamped frame is STRUCTURALLY DELETED at the V3->ISL boundary.
That is SAFE (ISL fails closed, no goal probability renders) but it is not 'it arrives'.
The consumer test this row will need must FAIL if ISL stops USING the frame — i.e. it must
assert the level->delta CONVERSION, not merely that the field survives the hop. A test that
proves transport is not a consumer test (see this manifest's own rule, and assistant_text).

fields.declared_in: schemas:src/graph.ts::ObservedStateSchema.declared_scale (0.31.0) — the declared scale of a factor value + DECLARED_SCALE_BOUNDS (ROADMAP 2.193)
notes: DECLARED. No producer stamps it and no consumer reads it at any pinned sha today.
WHY IT EXISTS AT ALL: ROADMAP 2.159 (normalised factors accepting out-of-range values
end-to-end, live-proven) could not be fixed by deriving the scale from the current value —
the #766 adversarial review proved that classification unsound in BOTH directions (a 0 or 1
is a legal raw count AND a legal proportion). 2.193 is the agreed fix path: DECLARE it.
VOCABULARY IS DERIVED, NOT INVENTED: the three members are the classes CEE's draft/edit
prompt SCALE_DISCIPLINE already distinguishes at draft time (bounded percentage / ratio
that may exceed 100% / small unitless count left raw). The knowledge exists upstream today
and is discarded before the wire.
PRODUCER WHEN IT LANDS: cee — the draft/edit transform that already applies SCALE_DISCIPLINE.
CONSUMERS WHEN THEY LAND: cee (value-edit authority check, enforce against the DECLARED scale
only) and ui (a min/max input hint derived from DECLARED_SCALE_BOUNDS).
ABSENCE FAILS OPEN, DELIBERATELY, AND IT IS THE ONLY 0.31.0 FIELD THAT DOES: absence means
UNDECLARED, which is every stored graph. Treating absence as unit_interval would be the
unsound guess 2.193 exists to retire AND would refuse legal values on existing graphs.
Backfill of stored graphs is a SEPARATE decision, named as such in 2.193 — not this train.
NOT A FIX FOR 2.159 ON ITS OWN. This row ships the DECLARATION only. The bound is enforced by
CEE's authority, and 2.159 stays open until that lands — pinned by a test in this release
asserting the schema does NOT reject 1.5 on a declared unit_interval.
DECLARED. Nothing produces it and nothing reads it yet.
DRIVING OBSERVATION (ROADMAP 2.225, 1 Aug): the LIVE bias coaching cards (2 per run, 3/3
captures, grounded and quoting the user's own brief) carry no action affordance at all.
action_intent and action_label were ALREADY optional on this block; what was missing is the
TURN TEXT, so a UI wanting a remedy chip had to invent an interpretation of a signal only
the producer understood.
AN UN-MADE DERIVATION GATES THE UI HALF, and it is NOT discharged by this release: does the
UI render action_intent on a `coaching` block at all today? 2.225 names that as step 1 of
the lane. This row must not be read as evidence that it does.
SCOPE: CoachingBlockSchema ONLY. ReviewCardBlockSchema and EvidenceBlockSchema also carry
action_intent/action_label and deliberately do NOT get action_prompt in 0.31.0 — extending
it is additive and should ride evidence of a real producer, not symmetry.
The consumer test this row will need must FAIL if the UI stops DISPATCHING the string, and
must pin that it is dispatched UNMODIFIED — a test that only proves the key parsed would
pass just as happily against a UI that re-composes the turn, which is the defect.
DECLARED. PLoT does not emit it yet; CEE and the UI do not read it yet.
WHAT IT REPLACES: consumer STRING-MATCHING of flip_reason, an open producer-owned vocabulary
this package does not own. A matcher on tokens like 'no_effect_within_bounds' is a
hand-maintained mirror — the day a producer renames or adds a token, every matcher silently
reclassifies a no-flip row as a flip row and the drift reads as green. The 2.228 work added
a new token to exactly this vocabulary, which is what surfaced the problem.
flip_reason is NOT narrowed by this release and must not be: it stays z.string() so the
producer keeps a human-readable channel. The boolean ends the MATCHING, not the field.
TRI-STATE, AND THE ASYMMETRY IS LOAD-BEARING: absence = NOT ATTESTED (every row on the wire
today), false = attested that a flip exists, true = attested no flip in range. A consumer
MUST NOT read `!== true` as 'there is a flip'. Recorded as a `distinct` row in the
absence-semantics census with the schema comment as its ref.
SAFE IN EITHER ORDER: a consumer may adopt before PLoT emits, because absence is the current
state of every row. But string matching should be deleted only once a consumer has SEEN
this field populated — never on the strength of the re-vendor alone.
